title: What Happens When Grouping Facts Quadruples What You Hold?
description:
Myth vs. Neural Mechanism — George A. Miller (1956): The Magical Number Seven, Plus or Minus Two & Cognitive Chunking, grounded in George A. Miller (1956) (Psychological Review). Empirical findings show that in 1956, George A. Miller opened his landmark Psychological Review paper by playfully joking he was 'persecuted by an integer' across two distinct cognitive limits.

At the circuit level, this episode examines how dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, parietal cortex coordinate behavioral and neural responses, alongside evidence that first, in unidimensional absolute judgment tasks (identifying pitch tones, loudness levels, saltiness, or pointer positions), human channel capacity hits an upper ceiling around 2.5 to 2.6 bits — roughly 5 to 7 distinguishable categories.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- George A. Miller (1956). The magical number seven, plus or minus two: Some limits on our capacity for processing information. Psychological Review. https://doi.org/10.1037/h0043158
- George A. Miller (1994). The magical number seven, plus or minus two: Some limits on our capacity for processing information. Psychological Review. https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-295x.101.2.343
- J.A. Morris (1992). Ageing, information and the magical number seven. Medical Hypotheses. https://doi.org/10.1016/0306-9877(92)90126-w
